name: náhuatl de Tehuacán-Zongolica

catalog_quote: El acento En todas las áreas dialectales del náhuatl, el acento de palabras de más de una sílaba recae ... recae, mecánicamente, en la penúltima sílaba . Asi- mismo, encontramos un número reducido de palabras acentuadas en la vocal final (Hasler 1995), por ejemplo: [ oksé ?] " otro ” ... acento carga en la penúltima sílaba de la palabra . Como excepción, toda la región de Tehuacán - Zongolica tiene el rasgo propio y distintivo del acento esdrújulo en un conjunto bien definido de palabras, a saber: 1) Sustantivos de más de dos sílabas terminados en -li o en -tli: [ tláškaļi ?] " tortilla " [ tlikónešti ?] “ ceniza " La lexía [ itskwíntti ?] (“ perro ") escapa a la regla ... Los sustantivos que han perdido -li siempre son graves ... 2) Sustantivos y adjetivos pluralizados con el sufijo -tin: [ tláškaltin] " tortillas " [ áyohtin] “ calabazas " [ míaktin] “ muchos " En contraste, en la misma región tenemos, por ejemplo: [ ayóhmeh] “ calabazas ” [ miákeh] “ muchos " 3) Agentivos singulares terminados en -ki, en contraste con el acento grave de los respectivos plurales: / teópiški / " sacerdote " / teopíškeh / " sacerdotes ” ... 4) Verbos en pretérito singular, de más de dos sílabas (sin contar el prefijo), terminados en -ki: / opálanki / = [ opálanki ?] “ se pudrió " / opalánkeh / = [ opalánke] “ se pudrieron ” ... El acento es predecible en casi todos los casos; sin embargo, tam- bién hay variaciones impredecibles .

new_statements.translation: ... falls, mechanically, on the penultimate syllable. Likewise we find a small number of words stressed on the final vowel (Hasler 1995), for example [okse?] 'other' ... stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the word. As an exception, the whole Tehuacan-Zongolica region has the characteristic and distinctive trait of antepenultimate stress in a well-defined set of words, namely: 1) Nouns of more than two syllables ending in -li or -tli: [tlaskali?] 'tortilla', [tlikonesti?] 'ash'. The lexeme [itskwintti?] ('dog') escapes the rule ... Nouns that have lost -li are always paroxytone.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls mechanically on the penultimate syllable of the word. As a regional peculiarity of the whole Tehuacan-Zongolica area, a well-defined class of words carries antepenultimate stress, the first (and clearest) class being nouns of more than two syllables ending in the absolutive suffix -li/-tli (the suffix syllable is skipped, so the stress lands on the last root syllable: tlaSKAli, tliKOnestli); the same nouns without -li revert to penultimate stress, and antepenultimate stress never reaches a pronominal prefix. A small closed set of words (compounds/enclitic fusions such as okse 'otro', ihkon 'asi') has final stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in the recovered snippets.
new_statements.exceptions: (1) Antepenultimate ('esdrujulo') stress in 'un conjunto bien definido de palabras', class 1) = nouns of more than two syllables ending in absolutive -li/-tli: [tlaskali] 'tortilla', [tlikonestli] 'ceniza'; [itskwintli] 'perro' escapes the rule (penult), 'probablemente para permitir la asimilacion silabica de la vocal inicial en cadenas sintacticas' ([se its-kwin-tli] 'un perro'); nouns that have lost -li are always paroxytone; antepenultimate stress never falls on pronominal prefixes ([ninehnemi] 'yo camino'). Further classes 2), 3).. exist in the book but were not recoverable from snippets. (2) A small number of words stressed on the final vowel: [okse] 'otro' (= ok + se, cf. Hasler 1995); [ihkon] 'asi' (aguda) vs [inon] 'eso' (grave), 'donde el condicionamiento del acento no es visible a partir de la simple comparacion sincronica'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (single words in phonetic brackets; one syntactic-chain example). The claim is explicitly region-wide: 'toda la region de Tehuacan-Zongolica', i.e. the Puebla Sierra Negra / Tehuacan valley varieties (this entry: nsu + npl) together with Zongolica/Orizaba Nahuatl of Veracruz (nlv); stress examples cited from Atlahuilco and Tequila (Veracruz) and, for saltillo/vowel matters, from Zoquitlan and Coyomeapan (Puebla). Text recovered from Google Books snippets (scanned): '?' inside brackets is the scanned rendering of the saltillo symbol; the exact page of the quoted sentence is inferred from the running head '45 EL NAHUATL DE TEHUACAN-ZONGOLICA' that Google returned in the same snippet as the 'El acento' heading.
new_statements.identity_note: sout3223 is Glottolog's bookkeeping entry for retired ISO 639-3 [nhs] 'Southeastern Puebla Nahuatl' (Tehuacan valley + Sierra Negra, southern Puebla), split by ISO change request 2006-089 (adopted 2007-07-18) into Southeastern Puebla Nahuatl [npl] = sout2973 and Sierra Negra Nahuatl [nsu] = sier1248. The only description found, Hasler Hangert 1996 (and 2001), treats 'el nahuatl de Tehuacan-Zongolica', a region that covers both successor languoids and also Orizaba/Zongolica Nahuatl [nlv] = oriz1235 in Veracruz; the stress statement is made for the whole region, with examples from Atlahuilco and Tequila (Veracruz) as well as Puebla localities (Zoquitlan, Coyomeapan). Any catalog entry should be filed under sout2973 and sier1248 (and cross-checked against oriz1235) rather than under this retired code.

No Tehuacan/Sierra Negra statement.
